title: Jio Platforms Wraps Global Roadshows, Readies Papers for $3.8 Billion IPO
excerpt: After investor meetings across the US, UK, Dubai, Singapore and Hong Kong, Reliance's digital arm is preparing its Red Herring Prospectus for what would be India's largest-ever listing.
body:
• Jio Platforms has completed the first leg of its IPO process after global roadshows with potential investors in the US, UK, Dubai, Singapore and Hong Kong, and is now preparing to file its Red Herring Prospectus, according to PTI, citing sources.
  • The issue, estimated at $3.8 billion, would surpass Hyundai Motor India's $3.3 billion 2024 listing and become the largest IPO in Indian history.
  • Sebi issued its final observations on the draft prospectus on August 28. The company plans to issue up to 27 crore fresh equity shares — about 2.9% of post-issue equity — in an entirely primary share sale that could value it at $137 billion.
  • Around Rs 27,500 crore of the proceeds will repay borrowings of telecom subsidiary Reliance Jio Infocomm, with the balance for general corporate purposes.

Jio Platforms, the digital services arm of Reliance Industries, has wrapped up global roadshows and is giving final touches to its public offer documents, bringing what would be India's largest-ever initial public offering closer to market, news agency PTI reported, citing sources.

"Jio Platforms has completed the first leg of the IPO after roadshows with potential investors globally. The roadshows were held in the US, UK, Dubai, Singapore and Hong Kong. Now, the company has started preparations for filing a red herring prospectus," a source aware of the development told PTI. Jio chairman and Jio Platforms managing director Akash Ambani, with Reliance Retail executive director Isha Ambani, led the overseas roadshows.

At an estimated $3.8 billion — roughly Rs 36,000-37,700 crore — the issue would eclipse Hyundai Motor India's $3.3 billion-equivalent listing in 2024 to become the largest IPO in India's capital market history. It would also exceed the proposed Rs 30,000 crore IPO of the National Stock Exchange, according to market estimates.

"Jio's listing will demonstrate to the world that India can produce a technology company of global scale, global standards, and global value."

— Mukesh Ambani, Chairman, Reliance Industries

Context & Background

The listing has been years in the making. Jio Platforms filed its draft prospectus in June, shortly after Mukesh Ambani told shareholders at Reliance's annual general meeting that the IPO would be the group's "most important value-creation milestone this year" and that his three children — Akash, Isha and Anant — would lead the listing. Sebi issued its final observations on August 28, clearing the key regulatory hurdle.

This will be the first public offering from the Reliance Group since 2008, and the first from its consumer-facing businesses. The shareholder base reads like a who's who of global capital: Meta holds 9.99%, Google 7.73%, and a consortium led by Silver Lake, KKR, Mubadala and General Atlantic holds about 15.2%. Reliance Industries retains around 66.4%.

Structurally, the issue is entirely primary — the 27 crore new shares represent roughly 2.9% of the post-issue equity base, meaning all proceeds flow to the company rather than allowing existing shareholders to sell. At the estimated size, the offering would value Jio Platforms at about $137 billion.

Impact & Analysis

The use of proceeds tells its own story. Around Rs 27,500 crore of the Rs 36,000 crore raise is earmarked for repaying or prepaying borrowings of Reliance Jio Infocomm, the telecom subsidiary. That is a deliberate deleveraging of the capital-intensive mobile business ahead of its next investment cycle — 5G monetisation, enterprise networking and an AI and cloud push. The remainder is reserved for general corporate purposes.

The underlying asset is formidable. Jio holds a 39.29% share of India's mobile market with 506 million customers and operates the largest 5G standalone network outside China, with 26.85 crore subscribers as of June 2026. It has expanded beyond connectivity into cloud, AI and enterprise networking.

Market conditions favour the deal. More than two dozen IPOs have been announced or launched since July 1, nearly matching the 28 recorded in the first half of 2026, with strong retail and domestic institutional participation. The risk is the macro backdrop — a $3.8 billion float needs sustained global risk appetite, and the choice of roadshow cities shows the company knows it needs foreign anchor demand to absorb the paper.

Diaspora Angle

This is a rare chance for the diaspora to own a piece of India's digital story directly: Jio Platforms will be a fresh listing with Meta and Google as existing backers and a $137 billion valuation benchmark against global telecom and technology giants. NRI investors tracking Indian equities can expect the issue to dominate index and mutual-fund flows on listing — and its performance will be a barometer for how global capital values Indian technology platforms at scale.

What's Next

The filing of the Red Herring Prospectus is the next formal step, after which the company can announce the price band and open dates. Watch for the anchor investor book, the final issue size, and the valuation investors accept against the $137 billion figure. For Reliance, a successful listing sets up the long-discussed Reliance Retail IPO as the next value-unlocking event.
